title: Recording: Bridge Over The River Suite by Wings; Wide Prairie by Linda McCartney | 1974
content:
Sound Shop Studio, Nashville
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Ernie Winfrey

Wings worked on three songs on 11 July 1974 at Nashville’s Sound Shop Studio, each of which was released by a different act: ‘Bridge Over The River Suite’, ‘Wide Prairie’, and ‘Send Me The Heart’.

Two sessions were held, the first running from 2-5.30pm, and the second from 6pm until midnight. In addition to Wings, in attendance were saxophonists Thaddeus Richard, William Puett, and Norman Ray, trumpet players George Tidwell and Barry McDonald, and trombonists Tony Dorsey and Dale Quillen. Dorsey had been commissioned by Paul McCartney to arrange parts for the songs, and the extra musicians had been hired by studio owner Buddy Killen.

‘Bridge Over The River Suite’ became the b-side of the ‘Walking In The Park With Eloise’ single, credited to The Country Hams. Wings had begun recording the instrumental at Abbey Road on 29 September 1972, during the Red Rose Speedway sessions. At that time it had the working title ‘Mood Music’.

The piece was completed on this day. Dorsey’s arrangement was based on suggestions by McCartney. The single was released on 18 October 1974 in the UK, and 2 December 1974 in the US.

The second track, ‘Wide Prairie’, had been earmarked for a Linda McCartney solo project. The backing track had been recorded in France on 21 November 1973, with additional overdubs recorded at Sound Shop Studio on 26 June 1974. On this day more saxophones and trumpets were added.

The evening session was devoted to the recording of Denny Laine’s song ‘Send Me The Heart’, which was released on his 1980 album Japanese Tears. Laine had written the song after being encouraged by McCartney to compose something influenced by their time in Nashville.

The recording featured Wings plus local pedal steel player Buddy Emmons. It was recorded not without incident: guitarist Jimmy McCulloch found little to do, so walked off the session. He returned to the studio control room later in the night, drunk, and threw a Coca-Cola bottle at the glass dividing the room from the main studio area. Buddy Killen threw him out, and the incident caused more tension on the current iteration of the band.
